sampling_model.design: Four-block strong-factor panel experiment with one unobserved counterfactual mean and a donor-only spectral construction.
sampling_model.units: For each \(n\), the donor block is \(n\times n\), the target row is \(1\times n\), and the target column is \(n\times1\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment masks the lower-right untreated potential-outcome entry; identification of its mean follows from the exact rank and span restrictions.
sampling_model.overlap: No target-loading lower bound is imposed; donor singular values satisfy \(cn\le s_r(A)\le s_1(A)\le C_0n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Known \(r\) and \(\sigma\); \(A\), its singular spaces, and both target loading coordinates are unknown and estimated only through the real Gaussian observations \(X,R,C\). The certified implementation first applies the measurable map \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\) and retains an explicit encoding-exception flag.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives Gaussian entrywise inference under condition \(4.4\mathrm{c}\).  The present upper guarantee removes that condition only on the canonical square one-target subclass proved by the embedding proposition; the local lower bound on this subclass transfers to any containing class because honesty on the larger class implies honesty on the subclass.
Theorems 4.1--4.2 give uniformly valid minimum-distance inference for first-order-degenerate smooth transformations from a uniformly Gaussian primitive estimator.
Appendix C proposes a first-order bilinear interval and states that analogous validity requires modified projected-loading conditions.
Residuals from computed SVD factors produce verified enclosures for singular values.
Truncated SVD has explicit first- and second-order perturbation expansions and normwise remainder bounds.

body.tldr: A strong donor block identifies the missing untreated panel mean as \(\theta_n=uA^+v\).  On an explicit bounded square one-target subclass of the Yan--Wainwright four-block model, the donor-only interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) remains uniformly valid through joint-zero and arbitrarily slow loading transitions, has expected length of order \(w_n=a_n+b_n\), attains the oracle Gaussian constant on every first-order-dominant sequence, and meets a local Kullback--Leibler length lower bound.  The subclass lower bound transfers to any containing class, but the upper theorem is not claimed for the full published class.  A measurable dyadic encoding followed by exact-dyadic directed arithmetic now has a certified matrix-sign, inversion, quantile, gate, and endpoint recurrence whose expected extra length is \(o(w_n)\); polynomial complexity for arbitrary refinable public-control names remains outside the headline theorem unless a known uniform query/output modulus is supplied.

project_justification.gap: Existing four-block panel intervals are sharp only after a target-loading lower bound, while generic first-order-degeneracy inference assumes that the primitive Gaussian experiment and its covariance are already available. Neither literature controls donor-SVD target drift at the quadratic \(n^{-1}\) width or certifies floating-point endpoints.
project_justification.niche: Known-rank Gaussian strong-donor panels isolate a finite-dimensional bilinear reduced experiment while retaining the repeated-spectrum, joint-zero, and arbitrarily slow-transition cases that defeat a single delta-method normalization.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the donor-conditional experiment, constructs an analytic outer interval with an observable donor allowance and bounded fallback, proves transition-order upper and local lower length results, embeds the statistical model as a canonical bounded square one-target Yan--Wainwright subclass, and supplies a complete exact-dyadic implementation theorem with explicit forward-error recurrences.  The statistical upper comparison is confined to that subclass; the subclass converse transfers upward to any containing class.

body.related_work: Yan and Wainwright (2024) supply the four-block spectral estimator, regular Gaussian theorem under condition \(4.4\mathrm{c}\), and a genie-aided lower-bound architecture.  The explicit augmented-matrix proposition here verifies their conditions \(4.1\)--\(4.4\mathrm{b}\) for a bounded square one-target subclass and shows that joint zero violates \(4.4\mathrm{c}\).  Thus the all-loading upper extension is claimed only on that embedded subclass, never on the full published class; conversely, a lower bound proved on the subclass applies to any containing class.  Bei and Navjeevan (2026) provide general first-order-degeneracy minimum-distance machinery from a primitive Gaussian experiment; the new work is the strong-donor panel transfer, observable donor allowance, and all-sequence length theorem.  Xia, Yan, and Wainwright (2025) and CAST are the direct same-question consumers.  Terao, Watanabe, and Ozaki (2025), Dopico and Moro (2004), and Vu, Chunikhina, and Raich (2021) inform verified spectral computation, while the present exact-dyadic theorem additionally certifies invariant projectors, residual inverses, gate branching, special-function quantiles, and endpoint padding.  IEEE 754-2019 supplies directed-rounding semantics; the theorem requires explicit rescaling and rejects overflow, subnormal values, and flushing.  No polynomial-complexity claim is made for an arbitrary refinable public-control name without a known uniform time-and-output-size modulus.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The certified implementation theorem uses exact-dyadic public controls \(\alpha,\sigma,c,C_0,B\) with finite descriptions.  A returned interval for a non-dyadic control can be propagated by the proved radius recurrence, but polynomial bit complexity additionally requires a known uniform query-time and output-size modulus incorporated into \(L_n\); an arbitrary black-box refinable name or one-shot interval is not covered.  The proof is a mathematical certificate for an abstract MPFR-equivalent directed model, not a formal verification of a particular software library.  The statistical scope remains known rank, independent homoskedastic Gaussian noise, exact span membership, and strong donors.
body.honest_scope: The statistical kernel assumes known fixed rank, known homoskedastic Gaussian variance, square strong donor blocks, exact row and column span membership, and fixed incoherence and entry bounds.  Its upper comparison with Yan--Wainwright is only on the explicitly embedded bounded square one-target subclass; it does not assert coverage over their full published class.  The local lower bound transfers to any containing class because a procedure honest on the larger class is honest on the subclass.  The implementation applies measurable finite-range dyadic encoding to continuous Gaussian observations and exact-dyadic directed arithmetic to the encoded arrays and public controls.  Arbitrary refinable public-control names require an additional known uniform complexity modulus.  No claim is made for unknown-rank adaptation, approximate-factor robustness, weak donors, dependence robustness, realized untreated outcomes, or formally verified production code.
